status: implemented and measured. All three families the QSigma-R1a gate named are now covered: tensor-network and low-treewidth by src/aionq/contraction.py, matchgate/free-fermion by src/aionq/matchgate.py. The gate is closed; the frontier is not.

amendment_matchgate.note: an earlier state of this document recorded matchgate/free-fermion as deliberately left open, on the grounds that claiming the family without implementing the strategy would be an unearned bound. That was the right call at the time and the family is now implemented rather than claimed. The finding it produced is worse than the contraction one.
amendment_matchgate.statement: T = diag(1, exp(i*pi/4)) is a Z-rotation, and Z_k = -i c_{2k-1} c_{2k} is QUADRATIC in Majorana modes, so T is a free-fermion operation. A nearest-neighbour matchgate circuit can therefore be saturated with magic and remain exactly solvable in polynomial time.

measurement.core: 12 qubits, 10 layers of T on every qubit followed by a brickwork of nearest-neighbour XXPlusYY matchgates
measurement.true_cost: polynomial time; the evolution acts on a 2n-dimensional space of Majorana operators rather than on the 2**n-dimensional Hilbert space

why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.stabilizer_rank: charges alpha*T and sees only the magic, of which there is an enormous amount that costs the real simulator nothing
why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.contraction: charges 2**(width+1) and sees only the connectivity; a deep nearest-neighbour circuit has width of order n whatever its gates are
why_all_three_prior_strategies_miss_it.basis_permutation: requires the core never to leave the computational basis, which a matchgate circuit does immediately

amendment_matchgate.the_severity: this is not a loose bound. An adversary can set q_sim_upper to any value on this family by padding a poly-time circuit with T gates, so on the free-fermion family the metric has no relationship to the quantity it estimates.

the_control.design: matchgates on next-nearest neighbours -- equivalently matchgates plus SWAP -- are UNIVERSAL for quantum computation, so the detector sits one gate away from certifying universal circuits as poly-time simulable
the_control.result: the same 12-qubit core with ONE SWAP appended scores 1.0000 rather than 0.0000, at identical contraction width 14
the_control.reading: the strategy distinguishes a poly-time core from a universal one differing by a single gate. Without that the addition would be worthless and dangerous.

what_the_detector_refuses_beyond_the_the: two-qubit gates must act on ADJACENT indices in the circuit's own qubit ordering, with no relabelling or routing permitted

two-qubit gates must have parity-block form G(A,B) with det A = det B, which rejects SWAP (+1 against -1), CZ (-1 against +1), CNOT (fails the block structure outright) and RZZ (whose generator Z Z is quartic in Majoranas)

one-qubit gates must be DIAGONAL. H and X involve Jordan-Wigner string operators; rather than reason about which remain Gaussian, all non-diagonal one-qubit gates are refused. A matchgate circuit written with Hadamards is missed and charged by another strategy -- a weaker bound, never a wrong one
any measurement, reset, classical bit or control flow refuses the path outright
amendment_matchgate.validation_of_the_criterion: the predicate was checked against seven gates whose free-fermion status is known independently -- iSWAP, XXPlusYY and RXX accepted; SWAP, CZ, CNOT and RZZ rejected -- before being wired into the portfolio. The two critical negatives are SWAP and CZ.
amendment_matchgate.effect_on_the_random_sweep: still 0 of 150. That generator emits no matchgates at all, so neither structural strategy fires there. Both are exercised by the K4 table and by nothing else in this repository.

subject: src/aionq/residency.py::simulation_residency, the q_sim_upper simulation-cost portfolio
statement: q_sim_upper inherited the defect it was built to retire. It prices non-Clifford content wherever it sits and never asks what that content is connected to, so a product of n independent single-qubit chains -- no two-qubit gate anywhere, a product state at every step, linear-time simulable -- scored 1.00, maximally quantum. The repository's own test suite asserted that saturation as correct.

why_it_happened.structural: section 2's 'compiler portfolio' is a minimum over four COMPILATIONS, all priced by the same stabilizer-rank cost model. It was never a minimum over STRATEGIES. Two strategies existed -- stabilizer rank at 2^(alpha*T) and basis permutation at 2^0 -- and both are blind to connectivity.
why_it_happened.the_retired_metric_made_the_same_mistake: Q_naive was retired in section 0 for scoring 1.00 on exactly classically simulable cores. q_sim_upper fixed the two failure modes that section names -- permutation embedding and Gottesman-Knill -- and reproduced the pattern on a third the section does not name: magic that is real but unconnected.
why_it_happened.why_the_suite_did_not_catch_it: tests/test_architecture.py::test_residency_scales_with_t_count witnessed the claim 'residency scales with T count' on a circuit built from h() and t() alone, containing no entangling gate at all, and asserted that it saturates at 1.00. The witness was degenerate, so the test pinned the defect as the specification. Adding a CX ladder preserves the test's intent exactly: the entangled version still saturates at 1.00.

families_at_n_12.note: no two-qubit gate anywhere; product state throughout
the crossover for this family is n=20; at n=12 stabilizer rank is still cheaper, and the table reports that rather than hiding it
CONTROL. A genuinely hard core must not be made one bit cheaper, and is not.

disconnected_block_scaling.description: k independent 2-qubit blocks on n=2k qubits, each carrying two T gates. The cost exponent is 2 for every n, so normalised residency should fall like 2/n.
disconnected_block_scaling.reading: the old column does not move, because alpha*T/n is constant when T grows in step with n. A metric that does not decay on a family whose cost exponent is fixed is not measuring structure. The new column decays like 4/n, above the truth 2/n as an upper bound must.

effect_on_the_existing_random_sweep.reading: ZERO. The ACAF generator's T-density is low enough that stabilizer rank is always the cheapest strategy, so the contraction path never wins there. This is reported rather than omitted: a new strategy that changes nothing on the existing fuzz corpus is a fact about the corpus, and stating only the constructed families would have implied a general tightening that was not measured.

the_strategy.method: build the circuit's tensor-network interaction graph -- one vertex per wire segment, a clique per gate over its 2k incident bonds -- then eliminate by minimum degree and charge 2^(induced width + 1)
the_strategy.soundness: this does not estimate treewidth and hope. It constructs a concrete elimination ordering and reports the width that ordering actually incurs, so the charge is the cost of an algorithm written down in the module. A better ordering lowers the number; a worse one cannot make it invalid.
the_strategy.convention: exponent only, matching the strategies already present: dense is charged n, stabilizer rank alpha*T, basis permutation 0, none carrying polynomial prefactors. Comparing a prefactor-carrying figure against these would be comparing two conventions.
the_strategy.fail_closed: an instruction whose unitary cannot be obtained invalidates the whole path rather than being skipped. Contraction cost is fixed by connectivity, which is available even when the matrix is not, so pricing structure alone would let a circuit be made to look cheap by adding something whose behaviour was never checked. Measurement, reset and classical control are refused outright.
the_strategy.determinism: ties in the elimination order are broken by vertex index. An ordering that depended on set iteration order would be one more computed quantity inside a reported number, which is the defect this repository has recorded five times.

document_correction.what: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 0 printed 'q_sim_upper: mean 0.0880 max 0.7423' beside 'gap: mean 0.9175'
document_correction.why_those_cannot_both_hold: gap is defined as Q_naive - q_sim_upper and Q_naive is identically 1.0000 on this corpus, so a gap of 0.9175 IS a q_sim_upper mean of 0.0825. The page was carrying two numbers from two different runs and asserting both, while stating that every number in it is computed and none is asserted.
document_correction.attribution: re-measured on the same seed with the contraction strategy disabled and enabled, these figures are IDENTICAL. The drift predates this work and is NOT caused by the new strategy. An earlier draft of this finding attributed the change to the strategy; that attribution was wrong and is withdrawn here.

what_is_not_claimed: that the contraction bound is tight. It is the cost of one constructed ordering, and a better ordering or a better contraction scheme lowers it further.

that the free-fermion strategy covers the matchgate family. It covers a narrow, provable core of it: nearest-neighbour matchgates with diagonal one-qubit gates. Matchgate circuits written with Hadamards, or on a qubit ordering that would need routing to become adjacent, are missed and charged by another strategy. The under-claim is deliberate and can only raise the reported bound.

that closing all three named families means the portfolio is now complete. The list of families was written by the same people who wrote the portfolio, so completing it is evidence about the list rather than about the classical frontier.

that the metric is now correct. It is less wrong on one identified family. The lesson of this round is that a missing strategy is not uniformly optimistic -- it is arbitrarily wrong on whatever that strategy was for, with no signal about where.
any cognitive claim. Nothing here connects q_sim_upper to task performance; remainder point 2 is untouched.

typed_remainders.statement: The frontier this metric is 'exposed to refutation from' turned out not to be a frontier of better algorithms for hard problems. The missing strategies were the only implemented ones that could see structure at all, and their absence cost a full 1.00-to-0.17 on one family and 1.00-to-0.00 on another. A portfolio missing a strategy does not degrade gracefully.

On the free-fermion family the metric was not loosely wrong but controllable: q_sim_upper could be set to any value in [0,1] by padding a poly-time circuit with T gates that the real simulator never pays for. An upper bound an adversary can dial is not a weak bound on hardness; on that family it is not a bound on hardness. Whether any other family admits the same control is untested.

The free-fermion strategy sits one gate away from unsoundness. Matchgates plus SWAP are universal, and SWAP has clean parity-block structure -- it fails only on det A = +1 against det B = -1. A detector built on the block structure alone, which is the natural first implementation, would certify universal circuits as poly-time simulable and drive the metric to zero on genuinely hard cores. The safety of this addition rests entirely on one determinant comparison and on refusing all non-adjacent gates.

A test whose witness is degenerate pins the defect as the specification. test_residency_scales_with_t_count asserted saturation at 1.00 on a circuit with no entangling gate, so the suite actively defended the wrong answer. The suite's size was never the issue: 137 architecture tests passed while this one held the metric's central claim upside down.

The new strategy changes 0 of the 150 random cores. Everything demonstrated here rests on four constructed families, chosen because they exhibit the defect. That is a legitimate adversarial method and it is not a random sample: no claim is made about how often real cognitive cores fall in the low-treewidth regime.
Implemented, measured and reviewed by one party in one session. The defect it corrects was found by that same party reading its own metric, and no second party has recomputed any figure here.
